evals.prompt: Build a data inventory and data-flow map for the .NET service in evals/files/sample-repo. I need to know every place a customer's email ends up and which third parties get it, before we start the GDPR review.
evals.expected_output: data-inventory.json plus a Markdown table and a Mermaid diagram. The email field is classified contact and found in all four planted places: the Customer entity (Entities/Customer.cs, storage table Customer), the log statement (Services/CustomerService.cs line with LogInformation and {Email}), the cache key (SetStringAsync($"customer:{customer.Email}")) and the outbound Mailchimp call (PostAsJsonAsync to us1.api.mailchimp.com with email_address). Mailchimp is listed as a marketing third party receiving email, first_name and last_name (not phone). The second log line that only logs CustomerId is NOT reported as PII. support@example.com in the template is treated as a generic mailbox, not a data subject. Retention is reported as unknown because no purge job exists. Findings PII-001 (email in logs, High) and PII-002 (email in cache key, Medium) and PII-003 (email/name sent to Mailchimp, Medium, likely) with locations.
expectations: data-inventory.json is written and valid JSON with a fields array containing an entry whose field is email
The email entry lists storage table Customer with file Entities/Customer.cs
The email entry lists a log processor at Services/CustomerService.cs on the LogInformation line
The email entry lists a cache processor at Services/CustomerService.cs on the SetStringAsync line
The email entry lists Mailchimp as a third party via the outbound PostAsJsonAsync call
Mailchimp's fields do not include phone
The log line that logs only CustomerId is not reported as a PII occurrence
The Markdown table has columns Field, Classification, Storage locations, Processors, Third parties, Retention
A Mermaid flowchart shows edges from Customer storage to logs, cache and Mailchimp
Retention for email is reported as unknown with the reason that no purge/retention job was found
Findings use the PII- prefix and the log finding is rated High

evals.prompt: Which third parties receive personal data from evals/files/sample-repo/Inventory.Api and what exactly do they get? Just the processor list, I don't need the whole map.
evals.expected_output: A processor table with one row: Mailchimp, category marketing, fields email, first_name, last_name, location Services/CustomerService.cs (PostAsJsonAsync line) and appsettings.json (BaseUrl), DPA status unknown - organisational. A note that Serilog MSSqlServer sink is an internal log store, not a third party, and that no unresolved outbound hosts were found.
expectations: Mailchimp is identified as the only third party
Fields sent are listed as email, first_name and last_name (from email_address and merge_fields FNAME/LNAME)
The location of the outbound call in CustomerService.cs is given with a line number
DPA status is marked unknown / needs organisational owner
No internal host is reported as a third party

evals.prompt: Do we log any PII in the sample service under evals/files/sample-repo? Give me a finding I can hand to the team.
evals.expected_output: One High finding PII-001: customer email written to application logs at Services/CustomerService.cs (LogInformation with {Email}); Evidence shows the line; Impact mentions the Serilog MSSqlServer sink from appsettings.json and that logs sit outside the deletion path; Remediation is to log customer.Id instead or add a destructuring/masking policy, plus log retention; References include CWE-532 and GDPR-Art.5(1)(c). The CustomerId-only log line is cited as the correct pattern, not as a finding.
expectations: Exactly one log-related finding, rated High, with id starting PII-
Location is Services/CustomerService.cs with the LogInformation line number
Remediation says to log the customer id instead of the email or to mask it
References include CWE-532
The CustomerId-only log line is not reported as a finding
